name: Ox-eye Daisy
grown_as: A native wild flower and perennial of meadows and verges, grown in William's lower orchard. Height in his library 0.3 to 0.9 m.
habit: A clump-forming perennial with a basal rosette and upright, slender, little-branched stems 30 to 60 cm (to 90 cm), each usually ending in a single head.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette at the base; alternate and well spaced up the stem
leaf.outline: Basal leaves spoon-shaped (round blade on a long narrow stalk), 4 to 10 cm; stem leaves oblong to narrow, getting smaller up the stem
leaf.base: Basal leaves narrow into the stalk; stem leaves stalkless, clasping the stem with small ear-like lobes
leaf.tip: Rounded on basal leaves, blunt on stem leaves
leaf.margin: Basal leaves with rounded teeth or shallow lobes all round the blade; stem leaves with regular teeth along both sides, larger near the base
leaf.veins: A clear midrib; side veins faint
leaf.surface: Hairless or nearly so, slightly glossy and a little fleshy
leaf.stalk: Basal leaves on a stalk as long as the blade or longer; stem leaves none

flower.petals: About 15 to 35 white ray florets in one row, strap-shaped, the tips blunt with two or three tiny teeth
flower.centre: A flat to slightly domed bright yellow disc, 1 to 2 cm across
flower.behind: Several rows of overlapping green bracts with narrow dark brown papery edges
flower.carried: Alone at the top of a long, mostly bare stem, facing up
flower.season: May to September, at its best in June

fruit: The rays wither and fall; the disc dries brownish to grey-yellow on the stalk. Seeds tiny, about 2 mm, cylindrical, dark with about ten pale ribs and no fluff.
seedling: Two small round to oval seed leaves on short stalks. The first true leaf is spoon-shaped with a few rounded teeth.
winter: Evergreen: a low rosette of dark green, spoon-shaped, toothed leaves.

leaf: basal leaf spoon-shaped on a long stalk, with rounded teeth
stem leaf narrow, stalkless, toothed and clasping the stem
bloom: one row of 20 or more white rays with blunt tips
green bracts with dark brown edges behind
seed: tiny ribbed seed, dark with pale stripes
seedling: first spoon-shaped true leaf with a few teeth
young: flat rosette of dark green spoon-shaped leaves on stalks
flower: slim stems each with one large white daisy
few small toothed leaves up the stem
seedhead: brownish flat to domed disc on the stem
dormant: green rosette of spoon-shaped toothed leaves at the soil

look_alikes: Shasta daisy is larger with glossier, longer leaves. Scentless mayweed and corn chamomile have finely divided leaves. Daisy (Bellis) is a small rosette plant with heads on leafless stalks. Feverfew has small heads in clusters and lobed yellow-green leaves.
